tier_terrarium.name: Tier Terrarium
tier_terrarium.description: A 3.30 m case holding all six members of the `tier` family side by side on one plinth, under one datum rail set at the height every one of them reaches at tier 1. Walk the tier axis and the row stops being level: by tier 5 the L-system tree stands at 3.000x where it started, the SDF grub at 2.969x, the mushroom and its posed twin at 1.857x, the CA colony at 1.750x - and the botanical flower at 0.668x, BELOW its own tier 1, because in flora:scatter alone tier is not a size at all but an index into a species table whose three species are not ordered by size. One word, six climb rates, spread over a factor of 4.49. The second channel drops the extents and shows only the mesh resolution the same number buys, where three of the six bays never change at all.
dev_themes: the kingdoms do not climb at the same rate
a bare number tells you nothing
interactions: read the row left to right at tier 1 - every organism tops out on the datum rail
walk the tier axis and watch the row fan out, then watch the flower fall below the rail at tier 4
switch to grain and see how many of the six bays the same number does not touch
tier_terrarium.capacity: SEE that `tier` is one word covering at least four unrelated quantities - extent, recursion depth, mesh budget and species identity - and that because each kingdom spends it differently, a single number in a map token means six different things at once and one of them runs backwards
tier_terrarium.qfep_connection: F is the number: one integer 1..5, parsed once by BiomeGridTokens.tier_of, identical in every cell of every map. E is what six dispatcher branches each decide it meant, and the six are irreducible to one another - a species index cannot be recovered from a voxel count and neither can be recovered from an L-system depth. lambda is how much of the organism the number is allowed to touch. The dark spot is the DEFAULT: 257 of the corpus's 344 declared biome cells carry no `t=` at all and silently take 2, so three quarters of the living world was authored by a fallback nobody typed, and the disagreement between the six readings has never had to show itself because almost nothing has ever been placed at any other rung.
tier_terrarium.relationships:
Synthesised out of the six artifacts that declare a `tier` axis, all of them living_* grammar tokens in commons/artifacts/registry/living.json - [[living_flora_bloom]], [[living_flora_tree]], [[living_fungus_fruit]], [[living_fungus_pose]], [[living_fungus_colony]], [[living_fauna_body]] - and out of the one file that turns their number into geometry, commons/biome_layers/biome_paint_dispatcher.gd.

UNLIKE EVERY OTHER FAMILY IN THIS CORPUS, THERE WAS NO WORD TO AGREE OR DISAGREE WITH. `removal` had gone|ghost|scar, `regime` had under|critical|over - words carry claims, and an artifact can refuse one on the record. `tier` is 1|2|3|4|5. A bare ordinal makes no claim at all, so it cannot be refused and it cannot be checked; the six members could not have discovered they disagreed, because none of them ever said anything a sibling could contradict. That is the condition this artifact exists to end, and it is why the finding is about the CODE rather than about the vocabulary.

[[living_flora_bloom]] is the member that breaks the ladder, and its own registry note half-knew: 'the tier ladder is really a SPECIES ladder here (bluebell -> orchid -> daisy); the gallery's flower strip found that. Whether tier should mean bigger or other is a ruling, not a default.' The ruling was never made. Measured, the answer is that tier already means `other` and it costs the plant more than half its height at rung 4.

[[living_fungus_fruit]] and [[living_fungus_pose]] are ONE dispatcher function, _spawn_fungus_preset (biome_paint_dispatcher.gd:472-502), reached by two three-line wrappers that differ only in which preset directory they read. Their tier ladders are therefore identical by construction, and this is the corpus's shared-vocabulary check working correctly for once: when a family word is honest the siblings measure alike. The artifact asserts it at run time rather than assuming it.

[[living_fungus_colony]] is the only member whose tier drives two extents at DIFFERENT rates: grid dim goes 9,12,15,18,21 while flat_y goes 4,4,5,6,7, so the mat spreads faster than it rises and tiers 1 and 2 are the same height.

[[living_ground_role]] is the seventh entry in living.json and is NOT a member - it declares `role`, not `tier` - so it has no bay here.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry - the case is boxes and cylinders at known constants, so this AABB is arithmetic: x = 5*PITCH + BAY_W + 0.06 = 3.30; y = 0 to PLINTH_H + BASE_H*3.000, the tallest organism being the tree at tier 5 (the grub tops out at 0.9214 and the tree at 0.9132, so 0.93 is the conservative ceiling); z = PLINTH_Z = BAY_D + 0.08. NOT a Godot measurement pass; re-measure when one is run.

dna.default:
channel=body, tier=2.

tier=2 IS NOT A FREE CHOICE, even though LAW 15 would allow one. BiomeGridTokens.tier_of returns 2 for any cell with no `t=` mod (BiomeGridTokens.gd:145-149), and a census of every map_data.json in the corpus finds 344 declared biome cells across 23 maps of which 257 - 74.7% - carry no `t=` at all. Add the 4 cells that spell `t=2` explicitly and the default is what 75.9% of the living world is actually standing at. A synthesis about this family that opened at any other rung would be opening on a rung almost nothing has ever been placed on.

channel=body IS the free choice, and it is the strongest single reading: it is the only channel every one of the six members participates in, it is where the flower's fall is visible, and it spans 44.72% against grain's 11.54%.

DECLARED ORDER IS channel THEN tier, and that is LAW 16 arithmetic rather than taste. build_dna_gallery trims from the END of the LATER axis's value list until the cross product fits the cap, and it sweeps only the first two axes. With channel first, a cap of 9 renders 2 x 4 = 8 frames and drops tier 5 - which is exactly half of the predicted closest pair, and leaves the default and the flower's cliff (tier 3 to tier 4) intact. With tier first, a cap of 9 keeps all five tiers and then has room for fewer than 2 channels, so the channel axis is dropped ENTIRELY and the sheet becomes a single-axis sweep with no notice given. The order is load-bearing.
dna.was: nothing. This artifact did not exist before this pass. Measured, not assumed: a sweep of every registry file returns exactly 6 entries declaring `tier`, all six in living.json, all six with the identical value list [1,2,3,4,5] and no reorderings.
dna.note:
WHAT `tier` MEANS IN THE CODE, which is the question the brief refused to answer and the answer outranks the artifact.

It is NOT the soft_stages.json progression. That file contains no `tier` key anywhere, and the curriculum gate is a separate and unrelated check against ConfigLoader.get_unlock_order at GridBiomeComponent.gd:353. It is NOT one thing either. `t=` is parsed once (BiomeGridTokens.gd:145-149, clamped 1..5, default 2) and then read as FOUR different quantities, and a fifth outside the organism:

  EXTENT    every kingdom multiplies some geometry gene by it
  DEPTH     tree L-system generations, CA freeze generation, mycelium growth steps
  DETAIL    the `lod` int handed to a morphology - and three of six are CAPPED
  IDENTITY  flora:scatter ALONE - tier indexes a species table
  STAIN     GridBiomeComponent.gd:363 uses 0.35 + 0.13*t and GridBiomeComponent.gd:1243 uses 0.4 + 0.12*t for the same ground presence, while the deposit at GridBiomeComponent.gd:724 carries t/5.0. Three formulas, one number, and the two stain formulas disagree with each other as well as with the deposit.

SO THE SIX MEMBERS DO DISAGREE ABOUT WHAT THEIR OWN TIER MEANS, and here is the disagreement as a number. Extent ratio against each member's own tier 1, derived from the branch of BiomePaintDispatcher that builds it:

  living_flora_bloom     1.000 1.118 1.404 0.615 0.668   t5/t1 = 0.668
  living_flora_tree      1.000 1.250 1.500 2.625 3.000   t5/t1 = 3.000
  living_fungus_fruit    1.000 1.214 1.429 1.643 1.857   t5/t1 = 1.857
  living_fungus_pose     1.000 1.214 1.429 1.643 1.857   t5/t1 = 1.857
  living_fungus_colony   1.000 1.000 1.250 1.500 1.750   t5/t1 = 1.750
  living_fauna_body      1.000 1.214 1.811 2.130 2.969   t5/t1 = 2.969

Spread 0.668 to 3.000, a factor of 4.49 across one shared word.

THE FLOWER RUNS BACKWARDS, and this is the sharpest single fact in the family. _spawn_flower (biome_paint_dispatcher.gd:215-243) uses tier for two things at once: it multiplies overall_scale by 1.5 + 0.20*t, and it looks the SPECIES up in biome_config.json:flower_presets_by_intensity, which ships {1: bluebell, 2: bluebell, 3: orchid, 4: daisy, 5: daisy}. The three species have stem_height 0.22, 0.25 and 0.10 m in botanical_flower.gd's PRESETS, and they are not ordered by size. Multiplying out: 0.3740, 0.4180, 0.5250, 0.2300, 0.2500 m. Tier 4 is 43.8% of tier 3 - a rung that is supposed to mean MORE removes 56.2% of the plant - and tier 5 never climbs back to tier 1. Five rungs, three species, and plateaus at both ends (1=2, 4=5).

THE DISCRETE LADDERS ARE SHORTER THAN FIVE, all three of them, and none of the three members says so:
  tree L-system generations   2, 2, 2, 3, 3   5 rungs, 2 distinct, never past 3 of an available 5
  fauna spine seg_count       4, 4, 5, 5, 6   5 rungs, 3 distinct
  flower species              bluebell, bluebell, orchid, daisy, daisy   5 rungs, 3 distinct
The tree case is the worst and it is caused by the SHIPPED CONFIG rather than by the code: tree_morphology.gd:76 computes clampi(roundi(segments * 0.5), 2, 5), and biome_config.json sets segments_per_intensity to 0.8, so segments runs 2.8..6.0, halves to 1.4..3.0 and rounds to 1,2,2,3,3 before the clamp lifts the first to 2. The code's own fallback of 1.0 would have given 2,2,3,3,4 - three distinct depths. The tuning file is strictly worse than the default it overrides, and it has never been noticed because nothing is placed above tier 3 in a map with an lsystem tree in it.

DETAIL IS MOSTLY DEAD, which is the grain channel's whole content. The `lod` int each branch computes, and the facet number it selects:
  living_flora_bloom     no lod argument exists on this path      12 12 12 12 12  (constant)
  living_flora_tree      lod = clampi(t-2, 0, 3)   0,0,1,2,3       3  3  4  6  8
  living_fungus_fruit    lod = clampi(t-1, 0, 3)   0,1,2,3,3       6 12 20 32 32
  living_fungus_pose     same function, same lod                   6 12 20 32 32
  living_fungus_colony   no lod argument exists on this path       4  4  4  4  4  (constant)
  living_fauna_body      lod = mini(clampi(t-1,0,3), 1)  0,1,1,1,1 6  8  8  8  8
Two of six bays have no detail channel at all; the fauna flatlines from tier 2 because BIOME_SDF_MAX_LOD caps it at 1; the two mushrooms saturate at tier 4 because clampi tops out; and above tier 4 exactly ONE bay in six still moves. Underneath all of it SdfMesher.RES_CAP = 34 truncates the SDF ladders again - the creature's RES_BY_LOD [24,32,42,52] can only ever reach 32 here, and its top two entries are unreachable from any tier.

A FIFTH READING NOBODY IS USING. biome_config.json:intensity_scaling.creature declares segments_base, segments_per_intensity, scale_base and scale_per_intensity, and _spawn_creature reads NONE of them - it pulls only mobility_base and mobility_per_intensity (biome_paint_dispatcher.gd:587-589) and hardcodes segments at 3.0 + 0.5*t and scale at 0.55 + 0.07*t (lines 599-600). Four of the six creature keys in the tuning file are dead, and the file's own note claims 'c5 = ~1.9x baseline creature' when the live arithmetic gives 1.452x on scale alone and 2.969x once seg_count is included. Neither number is 1.9.

MOBILITY IS THE ONE HONEST THING TIER DOES THAT A STILL CANNOT SEE (dna.mobility rises 0.5 to 0.9 across the ladder). It is not drawn here and is not claimed as an axis, per the brief's rule about time-domain axes.
dna.kin:
`tier` IS TAKEN, not refused, and taken with its value list character for character - ["1","2","3","4","5"], the identical list all six members declare. Refusing it was never available: a bare ordinal makes no claim, so there is nothing in it to be dishonest about. What CAN drift is the range, so the artifact round-trips every declared value through the family's own parser at _ready - BiomeGridTokens.tier_of({mods:{t:v}}) must return int(v) for all five - and additionally checks that '0' clamps up to 1 and '6' clamps down to 5. That is what proves 1..5 is the family's range rather than five strings that happen to look like it, and it is stronger than copying a const because tier_of is the function every map cell actually goes through.

LAW 2 - NEST OR SIDE BY SIDE, answered from the members' CODE. The KINGDOMS are PARALLEL: BiomeGridTokens.dispatch_kingdom_of maps them onto disjoint ints (flora 0/2, fauna 1, fungus 3) and BiomePaintDispatcher gives each its own _spawn_ function with no shared state; nothing about fungus contains flora. So the simultaneity is the object - all six stand at once, in one row, and the family word varies. The TIER VALUES nest, ordinally: tier_of clamps into an ordered range and every branch feeds it to a monotone expression. So tier is the axis and the kingdoms are the exhibit, which is exactly LAW 2's parallel case.

EXCEPT THAT THE NESTING IS A LIE IN ONE BAY, and that is the finding: flora:scatter's tier is an INDEX, not a magnitude, so its ladder is not monotone. The values nest in the parser and do not nest in the flower. Holding the kingdoms side by side is the only arrangement in which that shows.

`family`, `pose` and `algo` ARE REFUSED as second axes, on the record. Each is a real declared axis of exactly one member (fungus_fruit, fungus_pose, fungus_colony respectively) and none of the other five has anything to put at its values - four bays out of six would stand unchanged through the whole sweep and the sheet would be a fact about one bay published as a fact about the family. `algo` was the tempting one, because living_fungus_colony declares five values and living_flora_tree two; they share only `sdf`, so even that pairing is one bay's word.

`channel` IS THIS ARTIFACT'S OWN WORD and no sibling declares it. Its two values are not invented either - they are the two disjoint code paths tier reaches: dna geometry fields (scale, segments, grid dim) versus the `lod` int. See dna.predicted_relationship for the claim that keeps them disjoint.
dna.declines:
A THIRD AXIS `stain` REFUSED, and it is the most interesting refusal here. tier is read a fifth time as ground-presence strength by two formulas that disagree - 0.35 + 0.13*t at GridBiomeComponent.gd:363 and 0.4 + 0.12*t at GridBiomeComponent.gd:1243 - and a bay-by-bay stain would be legible in a still. It is refused because the two formulas do not branch by kingdom: every one of the six bays would receive the identical stain at a given tier, so the axis is INERT BY CONSTRUCTION across the thing this artifact exists to compare. The disagreement between the two formulas is real and is recorded in dna.note instead of being drawn.

`mobility` REFUSED - dispatcher:603 raises it 0.5 to 0.9 across the ladder and it is the one thing tier does to the fauna that is genuinely alive. It is a rate. The evidence here is one still PNG per value, so it is invisible, and shipping it would be info_board's fault exactly.

MYCELIUM AND SDF SUBSTRATES NOT DRAWN. living_fungus_colony declares algo [ca, dna, mycelium, sdf, softbody] and only `ca` gets the bay, because it is the most-placed substrate in the corpus (49 of the fungus cells against mycelium's 22 and sdf's 3) and because one bay cannot hold five substrates without becoming a second axis. Their tier arithmetic is recorded and not photographed: mycelium colony_radius 0.34 + 0.13*t, attractor_count (60 + 45*t)*density, max_nodes 150 + 110*t, max_steps 220 + 40*t (dispatcher:343-346); fungus sdf dna.scale (1.7 + 0.6*t) with lod capped at 1 (dispatcher:438, 458).

NO METRES ARE CLAIMED FOR FIVE OF THE SIX BAYS, deliberately. dna.scale is a GENE fed to a morphology, not a length, and this file will not invent the morphology's metres in order to look precise. Only the flower's ladder is in real metres (its preset stem_height is), and only the colony's is in real cells. Everything drawn is a RATIO against that bay's own tier 1, which is exactly what the code's linear formulas give exactly.

NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED NEEDED, and that is worth stating for a LIVING artifact in particular. The brief warned that living artifacts are the corpus's likeliest carriers of an unseeded randf, and the six real members are all seeded from cell position, which means five variants of any of them would be five different individuals. This artifact contains no RandomNumberGenerator, no randf, no randomize, no _process, no timer and no physics: _ready lays out a finished row from index arithmetic in one frame and it never moves. Nothing needs to be supplied and nothing needs to be pinned.

SIX FULL CAGES BUILT AND REMOVED. The first case gave each bay a 0.90 m frame of four posts and a top rail. Rasterised, it photographed as a picket fence: 24 posts of constant geometry outweighing six organisms, subject share 9.64% of which most was furniture, and the tallest organism reduced to a detail. The datum rail alone carries the whole reference, and dropping the cages raised the body channel's adjacent-pair separation from 15.79-20.04% to 36.05-42.53%.
dna.still_note:
READ THE Z-STACK BEFORE BELIEVING ANY NUMBER OFF THIS SHEET.

THERE IS NO GLASS, and for a thing called a terrarium that is the single most important sentence in this entry. operations_gallery's 'bezel' was one BoxMesh 24 mm thick that enclosed the panel face and every mark its axis drew, and it swept at 0.09% with the subject at 70.3% of frame - four photographs of one slab, every stage green. A terrarium with panes is that fault with a nicer name. The case here is a plinth, one datum rail and seven dividers, ALL of them at RAIL_Z = +0.15, the BACK of the bay. The z interval from the camera to every organism is empty.

ADJACENT BAYS DO NOT STAND IN EACH OTHER'S LIGHT, and the pitch was set by that arithmetic rather than by taste. The sweep camera stands at yaw 0.62, so a box of half-extents (hx, hy, hz) has a screen-x half-extent of hx*cos(0.62) + hz*sin(0.62). A bay's widest tenant is the grain column, 2*GRAIN_R = 0.29 m square, giving 0.202262 m; bay centres are PITCH*cos(0.62) = 0.472050 m apart. Daylight between neighbours is 0.472050 - 2*0.202262 = 0.067525 m, which is 14.1 px at this framing. Anything under PITCH 0.497 makes each bay stand in front of the next, and the first draft at 0.44 did exactly that.

THE SUBJECT IS AIRY, NOT SMALL (LAW 10). Rasterised subject share at the default is 7.14%, only just over the ~6% alarm - and the union box is 79.9% of frame WIDTH. This is taxonomy_hall's signature almost exactly (10.4% share, 75.7% frame width): six separated bays standing on a wide plinth leave most of their own bounding box empty. Do not tighten dna.framing on the share alone; the box is full across and thin vertically, which is what a row is.

WHAT THE TWO CHANNELS COST EACH OTHER: nothing, by construction, and that is the point of dna.predicted_relationship. body varies extent at the tier-2 facet count; grain varies facet count at a pinned height and radius. Neither reads the other's numbers.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS EVERY VALUE OF BOTH AXES. The plinth is identical at all ten variants and sets x and z; the tallest organism anywhere in the sweep sets y, and that is the tree at tier 5 in the body channel, BASE_H * 3.000 = 0.84 above the plinth top (the grub at 0.8314 is the runner-up, and the grain columns only reach GRAIN_H = 0.62, so grain never sets the box). Union 3.30 x 0.93 x 0.38, diagonal 3.449536, radius 1.724768.

THE RIG: FOV 34, PAD 1.9, dist = radius/tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing = 1.724768/0.3057307 * 1.9 * 0.555 = 5.948588 m, so the visible frame is 2*PAD*radius*framing = 3.637532 m and a 760 px still is 208.93 px per metre.

WHY 0.555 AND NOT 1.0: fit-by-DIAGONAL on a 3.30 x 0.93 body wastes most of a square frame - at framing 1.0 the row is 44.3% of frame width and 22.4% of its height, which is the thin-wide-subject case LAW 9 exists for. At 0.555 the projected width is 3.30*cos(0.62) + 0.38*sin(0.62) = 2.906590 m = 79.9% of the frame and the projected height is 1.471182 m = 40.4%. Below about 0.50 the plinth ends start to reach the frame edge.

EVERY MARK GAUGED AGAINST 208.93 px/m BEFORE IT WAS DRAWN (LAW 4). Grain column diameter 0.29 m = 60.6 px in the render and 15.9 px after the critic crops to subject and resizes to 160x160; mushroom cap 0.264 m = 55.2 px; colony voxel at tier 5, h/layers = 0.49/7 = 0.07 m = 14.6 px; flower stem 0.032 m = 6.7 px; datum rail 0.016 m = 3.34 px, which is furniture and not a mark. THIS GAUGE CHANGED THE DESIGN: the grain column was first drawn at 0.085 m radius, which is 9.7 px across after the resize, and the whole channel measured 0.195% - a fact about the drawing rather than about the LOD ladder. At GRAIN_R 0.145 it measures 0.88-5.78%. Note also the critic's resize is ANISOTROPIC here: the subject crop is 2.9066 x 1.4712 m stretched to a square 160x160, so vertical detail is amplified about 1.98x relative to horizontal - which favours this artifact, whose headline is a set of heights.
dna.predicted_relationship:
TWO CLAIMS, BOTH FALSIFIABLE, both stated before any capture (LAW 20).

(1) THE CHANNELS TOUCH DISJOINT PARTS OF THE OBJECT. body reads dna geometry fields and varies extent at a pinned facet count; grain reads the `lod` int and varies facet count at a pinned height (GRAIN_H) and radius (GRAIN_R). Under grain the six columns therefore stand at ONE height at every tier and the silhouette's top edge never moves. The testable consequence: NO GRAIN PAIR MAY EXCEED THE SMALLEST BODY PAIR. Predicted smallest body pair 36.05% (tier 4 vs 5), predicted largest grain pair 5.78% (tier 1 vs 2) - a margin of 6.2x, which is wide enough that the claim survives the 1.5x-6.7x under-prediction the rasteriser is known for. FALSIFYING THRESHOLD: if any grain pair measures above any body pair, the two channels are entangled and grain has borrowed extent signal; the first thing to check is whether _build_grain is reading _ladder ratio instead of facets.

(2) THE GRAIN LADDER'S SEPARATION IS ORDINAL IN THE NUMBER OF BAYS THAT MOVE. Counting from the facet table, the bays whose facet count changes between adjacent tiers are: 1->2 three bays (fruit 6->12, pose 6->12, fauna 6->8), 2->3 three bays (tree 3->4, fruit 12->20, pose 12->20), 3->4 three bays (tree 4->6, fruit 20->32, pose 20->32), 4->5 ONE bay (tree 6->8). So the 4-5 pair must be the smallest grain pair by a clear margin, and the other three must sit together. Predicted 5.78 / 5.72 / 3.90 / 0.88 - the three-bay pairs within 1.5x of each other and the one-bay pair 4.4x below the nearest of them. FALSIFYING THRESHOLD: if the 4-5 pair is NOT the minimum of the grain row, the lod formulas above were mis-derived from the dispatcher.

(3) A THIRD CLAIM THAT THE SHEET CANNOT SEE AND THE SCRIPT CAN. living_fungus_fruit and living_fungus_pose route to the same function, so their extent ratios must agree to 1e-9 and their facet counts must be equal integers at all five tiers - ten comparisons. _check_relationship asserts it at _ready and push_errors on any disagreement. This is the shared-vocabulary check the corpus keeps rediscovering: when a family word is honest, the siblings measure alike.
dna.measured: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-13 (second pass). THE VERDICT IS ABOUT THE HARNESS, AND THE FIRST DIAGNOSIS OF WHICH PART OF THE HARNESS WAS WRONG. This block previously read that the per-variant PNG write was at fault and that the contact sheet disagreed with it. Both halves of that are false and the sheet was never consulted: doc/reports/sweep_tier_terrarium.png from the same run shows five IDENTICAL body tiles and five IDENTICAL grain tiles, and the bite JSON from that run put every same-channel pair at exactly 0.0% and every cross-channel pair at exactly 8.017%. The sheet and the PNGs agreed completely. The reported 'peak 8.02% - BITES' was the CHANNEL axis; a live axis in the same sweep masked a dead one, because the bite line reports the peak over all pairs. THE REAL CAUSE: `tier` is declared `@export_enum("1".."5") var tier: String`, and tools/cabinet_sweep.py's coerce() tries int() on every value it is handed, so ada_run/sweep_spec.json carried "tier": 1 as an INT. Object.set() on a typed GDScript property whose type does not match is rejected in SILENCE - no error, no warning, no return value - so all five tiers were dropped and all ten frames rendered at the default rung. Proven independently of any image by commons/testing/probe_set_typed.gd: set("tier", 3) leaves the property reading "2"; set("tier", "3") works; the same int reaches `channel` as a String and takes, which is exactly why one axis moved and the other did not. SCOPE, measured across every declared axis in the corpus: 52 axes have all-numeric value lists and exactly ONE of them - this one - is backed by a String property. The six living_* tokens declaring tier as strings are sceneless grammar entries and are never swept. No other number in waves 2-7 is affected, and that was confirmed rather than assumed: re-verifying chapter_arc, opening_pair, grain_block and facture_bench after the fix reproduces 1.34% / 1.31% / 0.91% / 0.04%, identical to the committed values. FIXED in capture_config_sweep.gd: _coerce now converts a number to the matching member of a String enum (matched against the property's own hint, not formatted), and every assignment is READ BACK and recorded in <out>/_rejects.json, which cabinet_sweep.py refuses to publish over. THE AXIS NOW MEASURES. Closest pair 0.09% frame at channel=grain, tier 2 vs 3, subject 11.1% of frame; peak 8.51%. Adjacent body pairs 1.29 / 1.85 / 2.20 / 2.31%, adjacent grain pairs 0.36 / 0.09 / 0.38 / 0.11%. AGAINST THE PREDICTION, WHICH IS WHERE THE REMAINING INTEREST IS. The headline floor HELD: predicted closest 0.04% frame, measured 0.09%, 2.3x above. Relationship claim (1) HELD: the largest grain pair (0.38%) is comfortably under the smallest body pair (1.29%), a 3.4x margin, so the channels are disjoint as designed. Relationship claim (2) IS FALSIFIED on its own stated threshold: the minimum of the grain row is the 2-3 pair (0.09%), not the 4-5 pair (0.11%), and the predicted 4.4x margin below the other grain pairs is not there. The registry's own falsifying condition says this means the lod formulas were mis-derived from the dispatcher. Note also that three of eight per-pair predictions came in BELOW their number (body 1-2 at 0.7x, body 2-3 at 0.8x, grain 2-3 at 0.3x), which does not overturn the corpus law - that law is about the CLOSEST-PAIR headline, which held - but it does mean a per-pair table is not a floor the way the headline is. THE GRAIN CHANNEL IS THIN FOR A REASON THE ARTIFACT ITSELF GAUGED: a facet count going 12 to 20 on a column measuring ~16 px after the critic's resize is below the resolution of the still. That is thin-because-the-thing-is-thin, not inert, and it is left standing with the numbers on the record rather than inflated.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED CLOSEST PAIR: channel=grain, tier 4 against tier 5, at 0.88% focus and 0.04% frame. Rasterised, not guessed - all ten variants were built in Python from the same constants and the same derived ladders the script uses, projected through the sweep's own camera (yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, FOV 34, PAD 1.9, framing 0.555) at 760 px, then put through artifact_dna_critic's exact currency: crop to the UNION of the two frames' subject boxes (artifact_dna_critic.py:324-328, not either frame's box alone - cropping to one measures a different instrument), neutralise each frame's own corner background, greyscale, resize 160x160, mean of |a-b| over the hottest 5%.

THE ARITHMETIC FOR WHY IT IS THAT PAIR. At grain, tier 4 and tier 5 differ in exactly ONE of six bays. bloom has no lod argument (12 facets at every tier); colony has no lod argument (4 at every tier); fauna is capped by BIOME_SDF_MAX_LOD at lod 1 from tier 2 onward (res 32, 8 facets); fruit and pose both sit at clampi(t-1,0,3) = 3, so both are at LOD_CAP_SEGMENTS[3] = 32 at tier 4 AND at tier 5. Five sixths of the subject is byte-identical. The sixth bay is the tree, whose tube count goes LOD_TUBE_SIDES[2] = 6 to LOD_TUBE_SIDES[3] = 8 at the same radius, changing its silhouette width from 2r*cos(pi/6) = 1.732r to 2r*cos(pi/8) = 1.848r - a 6.7% change on one column that is one sixth of the row.

THE NUMBER IS A FLOOR, NOT A FORECAST (LAW 13). Every one of the corpus's four scored predictions under-predicted - 1.5x, 1.7x, 3.5x, 6.7x - because a Python rasteriser has one directional light, flat shading and no shadows, ambient occlusion or antialiasing. Read 0.88% as the floor for the closest pair and expect somewhere between 1.3% and 5.9%. THE RULE THIS BUYS: IF THE SWEEP COMES BACK BELOW THESE NUMBERS, STOP. operations_gallery predicted 4.18% and measured 0.09%, and it was the only artifact in the corpus to land under its own prediction and the only one that was rendering nothing.
